subject: Dedicated GPU sizing — traffic composition audit for Arclytic
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@arclytic.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arclytic Sales <sales@arclytic.ai>
Date: 2025-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing intake — sample telemetry and key workload notes

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a small sample of our API telemetry (arclytic_telemetry_sample.csv) covering a 48-hour window during a recent marketing push. High-level notes: we expect this pilot to run in the US and target a steady-state of ~450 requests/sec with short bursts up to ~2,200 req/sec for 8-12 minute windows (promotions).

Workload mix: approx 60% text generation (chat-style, multi-turn), 25% embeddings, 15% reranking/short responses. Prompt length distribution skews short: 75% prompts <= 80 tokens; the remaining 25% are longer developer-supplied system prompts (200-600 tokens). Response length: median ~120 tokens, but 10% of responses are long-form (>1,200 tokens) for our long-read generation feature.

Session behavior: sessions last 2-6 minutes on average, KV-cache hit estimated at ~40-55% for multi-turn chat. We also rely on streaming on the client side for long-form responses. Function/tool calling is rare but present (~1% of calls).

SLOs: customer-facing latency target p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 350ms for short responses; for long-form responses we budget higher latency but need throughput assurances.

Questions we want you to answer as part of the sizing audit:
- Recommended dedicated GPU sku(s) and sizing for an initial pilot that meets the steady-state and burst profile.
- Expected token/sec and concurrency targets to provision for to maintain p99 latency targets for short responses.
- KV-cache and batching recommendations to reduce unit cost without violating latency SLOs.
- Fallback strategies for overflow bursts (acceptable degraded modes).

Link to the full telemetry sample (CSV stub): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2bExample/view?usp=sharing

Attached: arclytic_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 480KB)

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform
Arclytic

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@arclytic.ai>
Cc: Arclytic Sales <sales@arclytic.ai>
Date: 2025-07-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake — sample telemetry and key workload notes

Hi Sanjay,

Appreciate the context and the sample CSV — this is exactly the level of signal we need. A couple quick clarifying items before I run it through our sizing workbook:

1) For the long-form responses (the 10% >1,200 tokens), are those produced synchronously on the same endpoints as the short responses or routed to a separate async job queue?

2) When you say KV-cache hit of 40-55%, is that measured across all chat sessions or only repeat-turns within the same session? Any example of reuse patterns helps (e.g., headline generation followed by multiple small edits).

3) Can you confirm the percent of requests that use streaming? Roughly how many of the long-form responses are streamed vs fully buffered server-side?

4) Any regulatory constraints on colocating customer data (e.g., dedicated VPC only) that would change node placement?

If you can answer those inline below I’ll fold them into the sizing hypothesis and loop in our pre-sales sizing team. I’ll also drop a short questionnaire for concurrency shaping and token mix so we can produce both a costed reserved fleet and an overprovisioned pilot plan.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks, Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@arclytic.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arclytic Sales <sales@arclytic.ai>
Date: 2025-07-28T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing intake — sample telemetry and key workload notes

Dylan — quick answers below:

1) Long-form responses are synchronous on the same endpoints for the pilot. We expect to move some to an async pipeline later, but for launch they must be served sync/streamed to clients.

2) The KV-cache hit estimate is across multi-turn sessions; most reuse is within-session (users iterating on the same draft). External repetitions (cross-session) are negligible at the moment.

3) About 22% of long-form responses are streamed; the client-side will render partial tokens while the backend continues generation. Short responses are rarely streamed.

4) No regulatory requirement for on-prem; however, Arclytic requires a VPC/private deployment option for enterprise customers in later phases. For the pilot, hosted in us-west is fine.

We also dropped a small sample of API logs to the shared Drive folder (same link). The CSV is annotated with request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, and session_id. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if that helps.

— Sanjay

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-28T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sizing intake — Arclytic telemetry + ask (pilot sizing request)

Camila / Priyom — forwarding Arclytic’s telemetry and clarifications. Key points we need to incorporate into the sizing hypothesis:

- Steady-state 450 req/s, promo bursts to ~2.2k req/s for ~10-minute windows.
- Mix: 60% generation (multi-turn chat), 25% embeddings, 15% rerank/short responses.
- Prompt lengths: 75% <=80 tokens; 25% long prompts (200-600 tokens). Response median ~120 tokens, 10% >1,200 tokens (served sync & partially streamed).
- KV-cache reuse 40-55% within-session.
- p95 target 150ms / p99 350ms for short responses; long-form higher but needs throughput assurances.
- Pilot region: us-west; no on-prem for initial launch.

Attachments: arclytic_telemetry_sample.csv (linked) — they also uploaded annotated API logs to Drive. I started a draft proposal (redwood_proposal_draft.pdf) with an initial reserved-capacity recommendation but it needs sizing math and SKU mapping.

Asks:
1) Priyom — can you run the telemetry sample through the capacity estimator and produce a recommended GPU mix (per-node SKU, expected concurrency per GPU, and expected token/sec) for both the steady-state and burst-case, with costs and fallback options?
2) Camila — please prepare a short attachment-ready explanation of KV-cache benefits, streaming implications, and a fallback degrade-mode (e.g., move long-form to best-effort async or scale out with lower-quality quantized variant).

Timeline: can we have a first-pass sizing deck by EOD Friday 2025-08-01? Arclytic is aiming to lock pilot capacity by the end of August.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a 30-min handoff if either of you want to walk through the CSV together.

- Dylan
